links.note: Qualities needed to fulfil a dream - determination, patience, readiness to face failure; that is the passion-and-perseverance theme, not the first-step confidence of 756
Discussion of Kalam's 'dream that does not let you sleep' - what a real dream demands of you, the central theme
What Ming must have written - doubts, fears and hesitation about taking the step; 756 is the concept about fear and the confidence needed to overcome it
How to reach international level - the ten-year, sustained-effort answer, i.e. perseverance and sacrifice
Asks what differentiates dreamers from achievers - the question's object is the paired contrast itself, which is 758; items about the effort alone sit on 755
How the mother uses 'critical questions' to provoke thought and persuade - that is 760's description verbatim; anecdotes are the secondary half
How she balances encouragement against caution - two opposed ideas held in parallel ('by all means follow' vs 'count the cost'), which is the antithesis concept rather than the theme
What costs of effort, sacrifice and time you would invest - the sacrifice strand of 755
seascape/cityscape/landscape are literal views while 'mindscape' is the figurative extension the exercise turns on - the literal-versus-figurative distinction of 769, not a theme item
Recognising the chapter as a heartfelt letter - frame recall for the letter that carries the theme; the set has no letter-format concept (763 is professional email)
The letter is addressed to her daughter Ming - frame recall of the advice text, same reason as the format item
What separates the key from the distractors is 'along with her doubts about the future' - Ming's fear, the substance of 756
'A guiding light' is a metaphor for the mother's role - the item turns on completing that metaphor, so 757 rather than the theme
The two things balanced are encouragement and reality - a question about opposed ideas in parallel, i.e. antithesis
The opening encouragement 'follow that dream' - the theme statement of the letter
The mother as a wise, caring guide - her guiding role in the pursuit of the dream; uses 'like', so not the metaphor concept 757
That the path ahead is tough - the sacrifice and perseverance the theme insists on
Ming's deep doubts and fears - the fear that 756 says self-belief must overcome
A simulated scene with assigned voices (Dreamer, Parent, Friend) and stock lines to use - the role-play task; 768 is the only role-play concept, though its lines are idioms rather than proverbs
Queen Madalasa passage matched to 'great personalities were shaped by their parents' - a parent guiding a child toward a goal, the same theme the letter carries
The ten-year rule for international-level skill - the perseverance measure at the centre of the letter
The fields named as examples of that ten-year rule - content of the same theme passage
'Count the cost' - the sacrifice the theme demands
A great dream demands a heavy price - sacrifice strand of the theme
Major personal sacrifices and financial investment are required - the theme's cost claim
Completes 'uphill task', one of the two idioms 766's description names; the distractors are plain adjectives, so the item tests the fixed expression
'Burning conviction' as what carries you through the journey - the passion strand of 755; 756 is about the confidence to start, not to endure
Definition of burning conviction as deep passionate belief in the work - same passion strand
Inner motivation keeps you on track when stamina runs out - perseverance
Inner motivation comes from the joy of doing what you love - the passion the theme rests on
Correct option is that success demands a decade of focused effort - the theme's central claim
The journey is filled with challenges - perseverance strand
Dedication must be continuous - perseverance strand
Completes the paired terms 'mere dreamers' and 'actual achievers' - the item is the contrast pair itself, so antithesis rather than theme
'Wishful thinking' as what goals stay at without effort - a claim about effort, not a question about the contrast, so 755 not 758
Achievers are willing to face obstacles - perseverance content, one side only, so not the contrast concept
Achievers turn imagination into reality - the theme's claim about acting on a dream
Dreamers retreat to a secure job when it gets hard - a detail about one side, so theme content rather than the contrast device
Achievers are ready to invest time and make sacrifices - the sacrifice claim of the theme
The item is about the distinction being clear-cut - the contrast as a structure, i.e. antithesis
Dreamers avoid tough sacrifices - the sacrifice strand; option D carries a stray page header, reported separately
Achievers are completely different from dreamers - the item asks for the opposition itself
World War II changed her friends' lives - the anecdote supporting the theme that dreams change yet the pursuit is worth it
The mother's own hard experience of publishing a book - the sacrifice anecdote inside the theme
Life is unpredictable - the lesson drawn from those anecdotes about pursuing a dream anyway
New evolving goals are as valuable as the childhood dream - the theme's view of a changing dream
A larger dreamscape brings a wider support system - the text's claim about pursuing dreams; the coinage itself is handled by the 769 item

The frame 'choice of course will be given to ___ applicants' takes the Latin expression bona fide, which is what this exercise drills; flagged as reasoned rather than certain because the stored answer text belongs to a different sub-item of the same exercise
